results.title: Ado's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra $L$ over a field $K$ of characteristic zero has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a natural number $n$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over $K$ from $L$ into the Lie algebra of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $K^n$ with the commutator bracket.

results.title: Ado–Iwasawa theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $K$. Then $L$ has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over $K$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over $K$ from $L$ to the Lie algebra of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $V$ with the commutator bracket.

results.title: Asymptotic count of cyclic and composite cyclic numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real $x$, let $A(x)$ be the number of cyclic numbers $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$, and let $cc(x)$ be the number of composite cyclic numbers $m \le x$, that is, cyclic numbers $m > 1$ that are not prime. Then, as $x \to \infty$, $A(x) \sim cc(x)$ and $cc(x) \sim x e^{-\gamma} / \log \log \log x$, where $\gamma$ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

results.title: The cyclic counting functions vary regularly with index one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real $x$, let $A(x)$ be the number of cyclic numbers $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$, let $\pi(x)$ be the number of primes $p \le x$, and let $cc(x)$ be the number of composite cyclic numbers $m \le x$, that is, cyclic numbers $m > 1$ that are not prime. Then for every real $\lambda > 0$, each of $A(\lambda x) / A(x)$, $\pi(\lambda x) / \pi(x)$ and $cc(\lambda x) / cc(x)$ tends to $\lambda$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: Taylor's law for cyclic numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c_1 < c_2 < \cdots$ be the cyclic numbers in increasing order, so $c_1 = 1$. For $n \ge 1$ let $m(c,n) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i$ be the mean of $c_1, \dots, c_n$, and for $n \ge 2$ let $v(c,n) = \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (c_i - m(c,n))^2$ be their variance. Then for every real $b$, as $n \to \infty$, $v(c,n) / m(c,n)^b$ tends to $\infty$ if $b < 2$, to $1/3$ if $b = 2$, and to $0$ if $b > 2$.

results.title: Mean and variance of the cyclic numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c_1 < c_2 < \cdots$ be the cyclic numbers in increasing order, so $c_1 = 1$. For $n \ge 1$ let $m(c,n) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i$ be the mean of $c_1, \dots, c_n$, and for $n \ge 2$ let $v(c,n) = \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (c_i - m(c,n))^2$ be their variance. Then, as $n \to \infty$, $m(c,n) \sim c_n / 2$ and $v(c,n) \sim c_n^2 / 12$.

results.title: Integer triples with square elementary symmetric functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ have square elementary symmetric functions when $a + b + c$, $ab + bc + ca$ and $abc$ are each the square of an integer.

results.title: Rationals with square elementary symmetric functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Rational numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ have square elementary symmetric functions when each of $a + b + c$, $ab + bc + ca$ and $abc$ is the square of a rational number.

results.title: Sums of two rational squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A rational number $q$ is a sum of two squares when $q = x^2 + y^2$ for some rational numbers $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Sums of two integer squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer $z$ is a sum of two squares when $z = x^2 + y^2$ for some integers $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Sums of two nonzero integer squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer $z$ is a sum of two nonzero squares when $z = x^2 + y^2$ for some nonzero integers $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Quotients of sums of two rational squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are nonzero rational numbers that are each a sum of two squares of rational numbers, then $\alpha / \beta$ is also a sum of two squares of rational numbers.

results.title: Self-similarity equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a self-similar compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$, then $\rho K^{(\mu)} = K$, where $K^{(\mu)}$ is the $\mu$-th derived set of $K$ (the set of accumulation points, iterated $\mu$ times) and $\rho K^{(\mu)}$ is its image under multiplication by $\rho$.

results.title: Layers of the iterated derived sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and a natural number $u$, let $K^{(u)}$ be the $u$-th derived set of $K$ (the derived set, i.e. the set of accumulation points, iterated $u$ times, with $K^{(0)} = K$). The layer of $K$ of index $u$ is $T_u = K^{(u)} \setminus K^{(u+1)}$, the set of points of $K^{(u)}$ that are isolated in $K^{(u)}$.

results.title: The zeroth layer is the set of isolated points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, the layer $T_0$ of $K$ equals $K \setminus K'$, where $K'$ is the derived set of $K$ (its set of accumulation points); that is, $T_0$ is the set of isolated points of $K$.

results.title: Layers of the derived set

Then for every set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and every $u \ge 0$, $T_{u+1}(K) = T_u(K')$, where $K'$ is the derived set of $K$.

results.title: Stable numbers for integer complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is stable when $n > 0$ and $\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$, where $\lVert m \rVert$ is the integer complexity of $m$.

results.title: Stable complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $\lVert m \rVert$ denote the integer complexity of a positive integer $m$, with $\lVert 0 \rVert = 0$, and let $a$ be the least natural number such that $3^a n$ is stable, with $a = 0$ if there is none. The stable complexity of $n$ is the integer $\lVert n \rVert_{\mathrm{st}} = \lVert 3^a n \rVert - 3a$.

results.title: Stable complexity of a stable number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $n$ is a stable natural number, then its stable complexity equals its integer complexity: $\lVert n \rVert_{\mathrm{st}} = \lVert n \rVert$.

results.title: The set $T_0$ built from stable numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a natural number $n$, and call $n$ stable when $n > 0$ and $\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$. The set $T_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ consists of the reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$.

results.title: The set $T_0$ is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every element of the set $T_0$ of reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with $\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), is a nonnegative real number.

results.title: The closure of $T_0$ is an arithmetical compact set (Theorem 2)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T_0$ be the set of reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with $\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), and let $K$ be the closure of $T_0$ in $\mathbb{R}$. Then $K$ is an arithmetical compact set of module $3$ and ratio $3$, and for every natural number $n \ge 1$ the stability gauge $\lVert n \rVert_K$ of $K$ with module $3$ and ratio $3$…

results.title: Terms of the modified Bessel series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m, k$ and a real number $x$, the $k$-th term of the series for the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $m$ is $x^{2k+m} / (2^{2k+m} \, k! \, (k+m)!)$.

results.title: Modified Bessel function of the first kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$ and real $x$, the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $m$ is $I_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} x^{2k+m} / (2^{2k+m} \, k! \, (k+m)!)$.

results.title: Modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $x$, $I_0(x)$ is the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$ at $x$, that is, $I_0(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} x^{2k} / (2^{2k} \, (k!)^2)$.

results.title: Modified Bessel function of the first kind of order one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $x$, $I_1(x)$ is the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $1$ at $x$, that is, $I_1(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} x^{2k+1} / (2^{2k+1} \, k! \, (k+1)!)$.

results.title: Bin packing instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of BIN PACKING is a triple $(s, B, K)$ of a finite list $s$ of natural numbers (the item sizes), a natural number $B$ (the bin capacity) and a natural number $K$ (the number of bins).

results.title: Feasible bin packing instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(s, B, K)$ of BIN PACKING is feasible when there is a list of exactly $K$ bins, each a finite list of natural numbers with sum at most $B$, such that the concatenation of the bins is a permutation of $s$.

results.title: The bin packing decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: BIN PACKING is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of bin packing instances, to a feasible instance; it rejects every bitstring that fails to decode.

results.title: BIN PACKING is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The bin packing decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.title: Step of a machine given by a transition function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be the deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with initial state $q_0$ and transition function $\delta$. For every configuration $c$, the step of $M$ from $c$ is the successor of $c$ under $\delta$: $c$ itself if $c$ is halted, and otherwise the result of applying to $c$ the action that $\delta$ selects for the state of $c$ and the symbols under its input and work tape heads.

Let $S_\delta$ be the map on configurations that fixes every halted configuration and sends a running configuration in state $q$…

results.title: Step determinism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, with the one-step relation it inherits as a nondeterministic machine. If a configuration $c$ steps to both $c_1$ and $c_2$, then $c_1 = c_2$.

results.title: Peeling off the first step of a run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the run from $c$ after $t + 1$ steps is in the same configuration as the run from the successor of $c$ after $t$ steps.

results.title: Halted configurations are fixed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine is halted, then for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ the run from $c$ is in configuration $c$ after $t$ steps.

results.title: Halting persists along a run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and steps $s \le t$, if the run from $c$ is halted after $s$ steps, then it is halted after $t$ steps.

results.title: Halting at step zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A deterministic multi-tape Turing machine started in a configuration $c$ halts at step $0$ if and only if $c$ is halted.

results.title: Run composition for halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a configuration of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$. If the run from $c$ is not halted after any $s < m$ steps, and the run from the configuration reached after $m$ steps halts at step $n$ (it is halted after $n$ steps and not halted after fewer), then the run from $c$ halts at step $m + n$.

results.title: Halting step after a run prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $c$ a configuration of $M$ and $m, n$ natural numbers. If $M$ started in $c$ halts at step $m + n$, that is, it is halted after $m + n$ steps and not halted after any fewer, then $M$ started in the configuration reached from $c$ after $m$ steps halts at step $n$.

results.title: A time bound forces halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine runs in time $t$ on input $w$, then the run from the initial configuration on $w$ is halted after $t$ steps.

results.title: Time bounds of deterministic machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $w$ an input and $t$ a natural number. Then $M$ runs in time $t$ on $w$, that is, every computation path of $M$ on $w$ with at least $t$ steps ends in a halted configuration, if and only if $M$ started in its initial configuration on $w$ is halted after $t$ steps.

results.title: Output determinism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A deterministic machine computes at most one output on an input.

results.title: Computing an output means halting with it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A deterministic multi-tape Turing machine computes the output $o$ on input $w$ if and only if there is a step $t$ at which the run from the initial configuration on $w$ halts (it is halted after $t$ steps and not halted after any $s < t$ steps) and the configuration it reaches after $t$ steps has output tape $o$.

results.title: Output at a time bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine runs in time $t$ on input $w$, then for every word $o$ the machine computes $o$ on $w$ if and only if the configuration reached from the initial configuration on $w$ after $t$ steps has output tape $o$.

results.title: Space of the deterministic computation path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input and $t \in \mathbb{N}$. The number of work-tape cells visited along the computation path of $M$ on $x$ made of the first $t$ steps from the initial configuration equals the space used by the run of $M$ from the initial configuration on $x$ up to step $t$. Both count the visited cells on each work tape separately and sum over the work tapes.

results.title: Space bounds of deterministic machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $M$ runs in space $s$ on $x$, that is, every computation path of $M$ on $x$ visits at most $s$ work-tape cells, if and only if for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ the run of $M$ from the initial configuration on $x$ visits at most $s$ work-tape cells within its first $t$ steps. Visited cells are counted on each work tape…

results.title: Relabelling the successor state of an action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a map $f : Q \to Q'$ of states and an action $a$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes and states $Q$, the relabelled action is the action with states $Q'$ that moves the input head, writes and moves on the work tapes and outputs exactly as $a$ does, and whose successor state is $f(q)$ when $a$ goes to state $q$ and is halting when $a$ halts.

results.title: Applying a relabelled action
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : Q \to Q'$ be a map of states; relabelling by $f$ replaces a state $q$ by $f(q)$ and keeps the halting state. results.title: Relabelling preserves halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a map of states. For every configuration $c$, the configuration obtained from $c$ by replacing its state $q$ by $f(q)$, and keeping the halting state, is halted if and only if $c$ is halted.

results.title: Every machine is a relabelling of itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes simulates itself up to the identity relabelling of its states.

results.title: Relabellings compose
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$, $M'$ and $M''$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet, with state sets $Q$, $Q'$ and $Q''$. If $M'$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $f : Q \to Q'$ and $M''$ simulates $M'$ up to the state relabelling $g : Q' \to Q''$, then $M''$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $g \circ f$.

results.title: Initial configurations under relabelling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input word $x$, the initial configuration of $M'$ on $x$ is the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$ with its state $q$ replaced by $f(q)$.

results.title: Lockstep runs from the initial configuration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input word $x$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration of $M'$ after $t$ steps on input $x$ is the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps on input $x$ with its state relabelled by $f$: a state $q$ becomes $f(q)$ and the halting state stays halting.

results.title: Relabelling preserves what a machine computes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for all words $x$ and $o$ over the alphabet, $M'$ started on input $x$ eventually halts with output $o$ if and only if $M$ does.

results.title: Relabelling preserves time bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input $x$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $M'$ runs in time $t$ on $x$ if and only if $M$ runs in time $t$ on $x$.

results.title: Relabelling preserves space bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input $x$ and every $s \in \mathbb{N}$, $M'$ runs in space $s$ on $x$ if and only if $M$ runs in space $s$ on $x$.

results.title: Relabelling preserves computing a function within time and space bounds
results.caption: Theorem

Let $e_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $e_{\mathrm{out}}$ be injective encodings of types $\alpha$ and $\beta$ as words over the alphabet, $g : \alpha \to \beta$ a function and $t, s : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ bounds. Then $M'$ computes $g$ with respect to these encodings in time $t$…

results.title: Relabelling preserves deciding a language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the alphabet $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every set $L$ of binary words, $M'$ decides $L$ if and only if $M$ decides $L$.
